answer: Latency-anchored admission via compute kernel timing. Each new identity must complete a challenge whose kernel runs only on sequential hardware cycles, so cloning requires dedicated silicon per clone. A vertex in the admission graph is granted only after the agent pays that latency once, and reuse is blocked by per-cycle nonce binding. The recurring cost is real idle compute; a walnut-sized pool of shared cores fails, because parallel cloning leaks timing and voids all derived identities.
